comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax implementation status
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD is continuing discussions on profit allocation and global minimum tax (Pillar One and Two), with the EU having adopted the 15% minimum tax for member states and many other countries implementing laws with effective dates starting in 2024, though some jurisdictions where the company operates have not yet adopted corresponding legislation.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose the implementation status of OECD Pillar Two legislation across jurisdictions. MU states that while EU member states have enacted the rules effective in 2025, other countries like Singapore plan to adopt similar legislation effective in 2026. AMD notes that the EU has adopted the 15% minimum tax and many countries have implemented laws with effective dates starting in 2024, but certain jurisdictions where AMD operates have not yet adopted corresponding legislation. Both highlight the ongoing global adoption and varying effective dates across regions.

sentences.text: Nearly all European Union member states have enacted the Pillar Two legislation, which will be effective for us in 2025.

While we do not expect these enacted laws to materially impact our effective tax rate for 2025, additional countries where we operate, including Singapore, have announced plans to adopt Pillar Two legislation.
The Council of the European Union has adopted the global corporate 15% minimum tax as provided for in Pillar Two and has directed EU member states to implement legislation enacting Pillar Two.
Many countries, including non-EU member states, have implemented laws based on Pillar Two proposals, with effective dates that started in 2024.

Although many countries have already introduced Pillar Two legislation applicable to us effective in 2024, certain jurisdictions in which we operate have not adopted corresponding legislation to date.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of Pillar Two on company's 2024 financials
comparisons.peer_summary: The impact of Pillar Two legislation on the company for the fiscal year 2024 was immaterial, and the company continues to evaluate the impact of proposed and enacted legislative changes on its effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD assess the materiality of Pillar Two's impact on their respective financials. AMD explicitly states that the impact on the company for fiscal year 2024 was immaterial. Similarly, MU states that it does not expect the enacted EU laws to materially impact its effective tax rate for 2025, though it anticipates significant expense increases in 2026 due to new adoptions like Singapore's. Both companies view the immediate or near-term impact as manageable, though AMD reports immateriality for the past year while MU projects immateriality for the upcoming year despite future risks.

comparisons.peer_summary: Singapore tax incentives provide reduced income tax rates on qualifying income, are subject to compliance conditions, and expire in November 2030, with the standard corporate rate being 17%.
comparisons.comparison: While both MU and AVGO disclose tax risks related to Singapore, the nature of the risk differs. MU identifies Singapore as a jurisdiction planning to adopt OECD Pillar Two legislation effective in 2026, which would significantly increase tax expense. In contrast, AVGO discloses that it currently benefits from specific tax incentives provided by the Singapore Economic Development Board that reduce its tax rate, subject to conditions and expiring in 2030. AVGO's disclosure focuses on existing favorable incentives rather than new minimum tax burdens, though both acknowledge Singapore as a key operational jurisdiction with tax implications.

comparisons.peer_topic: Factors impacting effective tax rate and variability
comparisons.peer_summary: Changes in the volume and mix of profits, business operating models, tax audits, deferred tax valuations, non-deductible expenses, tax credits, tax holidays, tax laws (including OECD Pillar Two), accounting standards, and repatriation decisions can impact the effective tax rate and cash payments. These factors may cause significant variability in financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC list OECD Pillar Two as a factor influencing their effective tax rate, but differ in specificity and impact assessment. MU provides a specific timeline, noting Pillar Two is effective in 2025 for the EU and will significantly increase expense in 2026 due to Singapore's adoption. INTC lists Pillar Two generally among various factors that can cause significant variability in the effective tax rate, without detailing the specific material impact or timeline in this summary sentence, contrasting with MU's specific forecast of a significant expense increase.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: While Pillar Two legislation has been enacted in certain jurisdictions starting in fiscal year 2025, it is not expected to materially impact NVIDIA's effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year based on current enacted laws, though new legislation could change this assessment.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA report on the impact of enacted OECD Pillar Two legislation on their effective tax rates, reaching similar conclusions for the near term. NVDA states that based on enacted laws, Pillar Two is not expected to materially impact its effective tax rate or cash flows in the next fiscal year, with legislation starting in fiscal 2025. MU similarly states that it does not expect enacted EU laws to materially impact its 2025 effective tax rate, despite Singapore's planned 2026 adoption causing future increases. Both companies anticipate immaterial impact for 2025/next fiscal year due to current enacted laws.

comparisons.peer_topic: OECD Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: The OECD announced a framework for a 15% global minimum tax (Pillar Two), with legislation in certain countries set to apply to the company starting in fiscal year 2025. QCOM does not currently expect a material impact on consolidated financial statements but continues to monitor implementation and OECD guidance.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM disclose that OECD Pillar Two legislation is set to apply to them beginning in fiscal year 2025 and that they do not currently expect a material impact on their financial statements. MU specifies that EU member states have enacted the rules effective in 2025, while QCOM notes that certain countries have implemented or are implementing legislation starting in fiscal 2025. Both companies express continued monitoring of the evolving landscape, with MU highlighting future increases from Singapore in 2026 and QCOM noting reliance on OECD guidance.
